newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bond spreads on tighter path again.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bond spreads on tighter path again.

text.p: Australian bonds re-established a tightening bias in yield spread to other dollar bloc bonds after Friday's profit-taking saw the market underperform.
Traders said the local market found a modest bid tone awaiting the outcome of Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting, but turnover was extremely thin.
The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread narrowed slightly to resistance at 110 basis points.
Last week, this spread briefly dipped to 106 basis points, its lowest level in over two years, although there was no trade in U.S. Treasuries in Asian time due to a holiday in Japan.
However, economists at Citibank Australia doubt that long bonds here can rally much further unless there is a clear indication of the Reserve Bank easing local policy again.
They believe such an easing, which would be most likely in November, could see 10-year bond yields fall to 7.50 percent with the spread to the U.S. narrowing to near 75 basis points.
